title: Model/Runtime Affinity: Pinning Strategy, Grace Periods, and Progressive Rollback Tooling
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem statement:
Customers and internal tenants sometimes pin a model version that depends on runtime behavior (serialization, KV cache format, kernel selection). When we roll runtime or model versions independently we risk silent correctness regressions or hard-to-observe errors (e.g., tokenization drift, cache corruption, attention kernel mismatches). Current routing falls back to the latest compatible model variant but lacks a formal affinity/pinning model, grace window, or a deterministic rollback plan.

Goal:
Define and implement a model/runtime affinity system that: (1) allows fine-grained pinning at route/customer/model-level, (2) exposes LTS channels and grace periods for runtime upgrades, (3) provides automated canary gates and rollback triggers, and (4) implements deterministic fallback policies across minor/major version boundaries. The design should avoid large manual cutovers and make upgrade behavior auditable.

Scope of this ticket:
- Design the affinity semantics and storage (how pins are expressed in routing policies).
- Implement routing-layer checks that consult a compatibility index before sending traffic to a runtime/model pairing.
- Add rollout gates: canary percentage, health thresholds (latency/5xx/regression detection), and automatic rollback triggers (severity, time window).
- Introduce a configurable grace period for model-runtime mismatches to allow background migrations (e.g., KV cache warming).
- Provide operator tooling: rollback button, migration preview, and a compatibility matrix UI endpoint for Console/CLI.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement full automated model retraining or automatic patching of model artifacts. It focuses on routing, gates, and rollback tooling for serving infrastructure.
acceptance_criteria: Routing supports explicit pin records: route-level and customer-level pins that map model@version -> runtime@version or channel (e.g., runtime:2.x LTS)
A compatibility index exists and is queryable by the router; incompatible pairings are rejected with a clear reason code
Rollout policy implementation with canary percent, time-window, success thresholds (p99 latency, error rate, quality regression hook) and automatic rollback when thresholds breach
Grace period mechanism that defers hard-fail on small incompatibilities for a configurable window and triggers background migration tasks
Operator UI/CLI exposes: compatibility matrix, active pins, option to force-failover or rollback, and a migration dry-run report
End-to-end test harness that validates at least three downgrade/upgrade scenarios (minor upgrade, major upgrade with translation layer, forced rollback)
tasks: Design: draft affinity spec and pinning grammar (Priya)
Routing: add compatibility check to request path and error codes (Marco)
Index: build a simple compatibility catalog service and API (runtime team)
Gates: implement canary rollout engine and automatic rollback hooks tied to metrics (SRE)
Console: add read-only compatibility view and quick-rollback action (Frontend)
Tests: add integration tests simulating KV cache incompatibility and tokenization mismatch (QA)
Runbook: write an operator runbook including troubleshooting and rollback procedures
comments: 2025-02-12 Priya: Initial spec uploaded to Confluence. Requesting feedback from runtime and SRE on compatibility signals.
2025-02-18 Marco: Prototype compatibility check added to local router. It rejects incompatible pairs with ERROR_CODE:COMPAT_MISMATCH. Needs catalog API integration.
2025-02-21 SRE (Ana Gomez): Suggested adding a secondary signal for quality regressions (eval-based) — added quality webhook to rollout gate design.
2025-02-25 Design review: Frontend can show a matrix but needs an API endpoint that returns pin provenance and last migration timestamp.
2025-02-28 QA (Hassan): Added tests for a simulated tokenization version mismatch; observed graceful degradation when grace_period=10m.
2025-03-01 Marco: Wiring to compatibility catalog done; canary rollout engine integrated. Next: Console UI and runbook.
notes: Compatibility catalog model: CSV-backed at first, migrate to ConfigDB once schema stabilizes
Grace period default proposed: 10 minutes for minor mismatches, 24 hours for migration-needed major mismatches
Fallback policy: prefer nearest compatible runtime version within same LTS channel; otherwise route to read-only safe path (reject write operations)
Metrics to watch: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, eval-score-drift (quality), and kv-cache-miss-rate
discussion: Question: Should we allow model pins to reference a runtime channel (runtime:2.x-LTS) instead of exact runtime@semver? Decision: support both; channel pins default to latest within that channel unless explicit lock is set.
Question: How do we handle binary format changes for KV cache? Proposed: include cache-format-version in compatibility index and surface migration helpers that can pre-warm caches.
Suggestion: Add a migration dry-run mode that simulates requests against a candidate runtime but routes real traffic unchanged; used to detect regressions before increasing canary percent.
